prerequisites: Knowledge of the structure of inorganic, especially metallic materials, and understanding of materials science terms.
Understanding of the thermodynamic relationships of energy forms.
Understanding of what is represented in a phase diagram.
High school level knowledge of Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics.
Knowledge and application of basic programming (variables, data types, loops).
Successful completion of the Study Entrance and Orientation Phase (StEOP).

learning_outcomes.text: Describe the various areas of computer-aided material modeling and apply them in simple case studies.
Perform initial calculations to derive or predict fundamental aspects of the stability and development of a material and its microstructure.
Contrast the stability of a material with transformation processes.
Demonstrate the essential role of computer-aided material modeling.
Critically evaluate existing models and predictions.
Recognize the limits of model extrapolations and contrast their validity ranges and applicability.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to atomistic modeling in the context of materials science.
Introduction, definition, and use of interatomic potentials.
Methods based on variable length scales.
Learning, understanding, and applying Electronic Structure Calculations and Density Functional Theory.
Introduction to thermodynamic state variables and their functions in semi-empirical, thermodynamic mixtures, and physically-based models.
Creation of thermodynamic databases for calculating and interpreting phase diagrams and property diagrams.
Introduction to and learning of data-driven models for utilizing data from simulations and experiments to learn correlations between structure, process, and properties.
Introduction to and learning of hybrid approaches that incorporate physical laws into data-driven approaches to increase prediction accuracy even with limited data.
Application of data science and computer science methods to materials science problems.
Learning how to generate data, build databases, and standardize data to ensure machine readability.
Preparation of unstructured data, selection of relevant descriptors (e.g., electron structure, molecular graphs) for describing materials.
teaching_methods: Lectures, supported with PowerPoint slides, whiteboard, and blackboard work.
Collaborative development of models and parameterizations on the computer in small teams.
Team/group work on practical case studies with subsequent discussion for illustration.
Brief summary of the previous lecture unit at the beginning of each session, with opportunity for students to clarify ambiguities and ask in-depth questions.
Short question rounds at the end of each lecture unit.

assessment_methods.method: Protocols and reports for completed case studies

assessment_rules: Performance will be assessed through written and/or oral examination, or protocols and reports for completed case studies. Assessment also includes regular homework assignments, class participation, and interim tests. The specific examination modalities will be announced in the information system for studies and teaching before the start of the semester for each course.
